role.altitude: The farm equipment mechanic keeps diagnosing by eye and ear, talking with farmers and repairing; filling paper job cards, looking up part prices and adding up bills shrink.
skills_to_grow: Recording time and parts on the job in the work order app
role.ambitious_version: A mechanic whose job is billed the evening it is finished, without anyone retyping a card.

tasks.short: Take the farmer's report, confer with customers about symptoms, read inspection reports and the machine's history, read fault codes, examine and listen to equipment to locate and diagnose malfunctions, and look up manuals.

steps.what: Farmer reports the problem by phone
Mechanic confers with the customer about the symptoms at the farm or the workshop
Mechanic reads inspection reports and the machine's service history
Mechanic reads fault codes with the manufacturer's diagnostic tool
Mechanic examines and listens to the equipment and tests it to locate and diagnose the malfunction
Mechanic looks up service manuals and known fixes

tasks.design: Diagnosis stays hands-on. The only changes: the machine's service history from earlier work orders and the last inspection report show on the mechanic's tablet by serial number instead of in paper files, and on connected machines the fault codes reported by the machine arrive with the job, so some are known before the visit.
tasks.previous_blocker: History was in paper job cards at the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Work order apps that keep history per machine serial, and machines that report fault codes.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults that show only in the field under load.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a bearing going before it fails.

reach.learn: Whether fault codes sent ahead shorten farm visits.

evidence.claim: A work order platform covers the flow from job to invoice.
Modern farm machines report fault codes to the manufacturer's portal.

assumptions: Boundary: from the farmer's report to the diagnosis and repair method; the repair is outside.
Input contract for s3: closed work orders recorded by mechanics in the app (see the repair records task) and inspection reports filed per serial number; older paper history is not scanned.
Input contract for s4: fault codes from the manufacturer's portal for connected machines, about a third of the fleet served.
Talking, examining and testing keep their full time; the farmer's time is outside the mechanic's savings.
unknowns: Share of connected machines among customers.
research_questions: Do repeat visits for the same fault fall?

incremental.description: Mechanic checks that the machine serial on the job matches the machine.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older machines without telematics; high: newer connected fleets with full history in the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record details of repairs made, time and parts used on the job, write findings and advice, hand in the job and have it in the dealer system.

steps.what: Mechanic records details of repairs made and hours on the paper job card
Mechanic writes the parts used with part numbers
Mechanic writes findings and advice for the customer
Mechanic hands in the job card at the workshop office
Workshop administrator types the job card into the dealer system

tasks.design: The job is a work order in an app on the mechanic's phone or tablet. The mechanic taps start and stop on the job so actual hours are captured, picks operations from a list, scans the barcodes of parts taken from van or warehouse stock, and types or dictates findings and advice. Closing the job syncs it into the dealer system ({ERP}), so no paper card is carried in or retyped.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job cards were filled by hand and typed in at the office, often days later.
tasks.enabler_now: Work order apps that take time stamps and part scans and sync to the dealer system.
tasks.still_hard: Remembering to stop the clock when called away to another job.
tasks.human_edge: Writing advice the farmer will act on.
tasks.altitude: Less writing; the record is the mechanic's own as before.

reach.learn: Whether synced jobs end retyping and missing cards.

evidence.claim: A Dutch work order platform covers the flow from job to invoice, with the accounting package used for invoicing.
In a vendor's parallel run, a paper maintenance log had 52 errors in two months against 1 in the electronic log (aircraft, not farm machines).
Time stamps used to watch mechanics' speed need works council consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: recording a finished repair; billing is a separate task.
Input contract for s1: actual start and stop times tapped by the mechanic on the job; the app does not track location.
Input contract for s2: barcodes on parts from the manufacturer and the dealer's warehouse labels, on about 80% of parts; the rest are typed; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s5: the app's sync to the dealer system set up by the supplier.
Time stamps are not used to rate mechanics; administrator time is outside the mechanic's savings.
unknowns: Whether the dealer system has a work order app.

already_counted.description: Mechanic corrects forgotten start or stop taps before closing the job.

incremental.description: Mechanic keeps the device charged and synced.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: farm visits with poor signal and many unlabelled parts; high: workshop jobs with labelled stock parts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate bills according to the record of repairs made, labor time and parts used: add hours, price parts, add travel and VAT, check against the quote, have the bill approved, post it to accounting and send it to the farmer.

steps.what: Mechanic adds up labor time from the job record and multiplies by the rate
Mechanic looks up prices of parts used and adds them to the bill
Mechanic adds travel, small materials and VAT
Mechanic checks the bill against the quote and agreements with the farmer
Service manager approves the final bill
Mechanic types the approved bill into the accounting package
Mechanic mails the bill to the farmer

approvals.approved_version: the bill as approved by the service manager in s5; any change goes back for approval
the bill as approved by the service manager in s5 and posted in s6; any change goes back for approval

tasks.design: When the job closes, the work order holds the actual hours and scanned parts. Fixed rules multiply hours by the rate, price parts from the dealer's price file, add travel by zone and small materials, and apply VAT, producing a draft bill. The mechanic checks it against the quote, the service manager approves it, and the approved bill posts to the accounting package through the work order link and is e-mailed to the farmer from there, each as its own step after approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bills were added up from paper cards and price lists and typed into accounting.
tasks.enabler_now: Work order systems that price jobs and post invoices to accounting.
tasks.still_hard: Goodwill and warranty splits agreed on the phone.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a long-standing customer gets a discount.
tasks.altitude: Most adding up goes; pricing decisions stay with people.

reach.learn: Whether price file errors show up on bills.

evidence.claim: A Dutch work order platform covers job to invoice, with the accounting package used for post-calculation and invoicing at one customer.
Bills drawn from closed work orders need no model; fixed rules do the calculation.

assumptions: Boundary: from the closed job record to the bill sent; payment follow-up is outside.
Input contract for s1: actual hours captured by the mechanic in the work order app on about 85% of jobs; the rest come from paper cards; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: parts scanned on the job and the dealer's price file imported from the manufacturers' price lists by the parts department; about 80% of lines priced automatically.
Input contract for s6 and s7: the work order system's link to the accounting package and its mail function; about 10% of customers want paper bills.
The quote check keeps most of its time; the service manager's approval is outside the mechanic's savings.
unknowns: Who bills at this dealer: mechanic, workshop manager or office.

already_counted.description: Mechanic checks bill lines for jobs with unscanned parts or missing hours.

incremental.description: Parts department imports the manufacturers' price lists.
Mechanic reports wrong rates or travel zones to the service manager.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many field jobs on paper cards and unscanned parts; high: workshop jobs fully recorded in the app.
